title: Waffles and Pip Investigate the Garden

pages.alt: Waffles wears his detective lettuce hat and inspects a ripe tomato while Pip watches.
pages.text:
Waffles the white rabbit stood at the edge of the garden.

He wore a leaf on his head.

Pip the little blue bird landed beside him.

“Why are you wearing that?”

“It is my detective hat.”

“It is lettuce.”

“Detective lettuce.”

Pip sighed.

Waffles pointed toward the garden.

“Something suspicious is happening.”

pages.alt: Waffles wears his detective lettuce hat and inspects a ripe tomato while Pip watches.
pages.text:
Pip looked around.

The flowers were blooming.

The bees were buzzing.

The sun was shining.

A ladybug walked across a leaf.

“What is suspicious?”

Waffles whispered,

“Everything.”

Pip blinked.

“That seems like a lot.”

Waffles hopped into the garden.

“Investigation begins NOW.”

pages.alt: Waffles wears his detective lettuce hat and inspects a ripe tomato while Pip watches.
pages.text:
First, they examined the tomatoes.

Waffles stared at one.

The tomato stared back.

At least Waffles thought it did.

“Very suspicious.”

“It’s a tomato.”

“It is red.”

“Yes.”

“Why?”

“Because it is ripe.”

pages.alt: Waffles wears his detective lettuce hat and inspects a ripe tomato while Pip watches.
pages.text:
Waffles narrowed his eyes.

“That is exactly what a suspicious tomato would say.”

“The tomato didn’t say anything.”

“Even more suspicious.”

Pip flew to the next garden row.

“Come look at this.”

Waffles hurried over.

There were tiny holes in the lettuce leaves.

Waffles gasped.

“THE CRIMINAL HAS STRUCK.”

pages.alt: Waffles and Pip discover a tiny green caterpillar nibbling lettuce.
pages.text:
Pip leaned closer.

“Looks like something has been nibbling.”

Waffles looked horrified.

“NIBBLING?”

He turned slowly.

“Who would do such a thing?”

Pip stared at him.

Waffles stared back.

Pip looked at his mouth.

A little piece of lettuce was stuck to his lip.

Waffles quickly swallowed it.

“That proves nothing.”

pages.alt: Waffles and Pip discover a tiny green caterpillar nibbling lettuce.
pages.text:
They searched for clues.

Pip found a tiny green caterpillar.

Waffles crouched beside it.

“State your name.”

The caterpillar kept eating.

“Where were you last night?”

The caterpillar kept eating.

“Do you have an alibi?”

Crunch.

Crunch.

Crunch.

pages.alt: Waffles and Pip discover a tiny green caterpillar nibbling lettuce.
pages.text:
Pip laughed.

“I think you found your lettuce nibbler.”

Waffles gasped.

“The suspect is still eating the evidence!”

The caterpillar crawled onto another leaf.

Waffles whispered,

“Bold.”

Pip gently moved the caterpillar to a patch of wild plants outside the garden.

“Problem solved.”

Waffles puffed out his chest.

“Excellent detective work.”

“You didn’t do anything.”

“I supervised.”

pages.alt: A friendly mole emerges from a mound beside the carrots, surprising Waffles.
pages.text:
They continued.

Near the carrots, they found a small mound of dirt.

Waffles froze.

“Pip.”

“Yes?”

“There has been digging.”

Pip looked at him.

“You dig all the time.”

“Exactly.”

Waffles looked around nervously.

“There may be another rabbit.”

Pip tilted her head.

“You are worried about another rabbit?”

“No.”

Waffles paused.

“Yes.”

pages.alt: A friendly mole emerges from a mound beside the carrots, surprising Waffles.
pages.text:
A tiny nose popped out of the dirt.

Waffles jumped backward.

“AAAH!”

A mole climbed out.

The mole blinked.

Waffles blinked.

Pip blinked.

The mole said,

“Hello.”

Waffles whispered,

“He talks.”

“So do you,” said Pip.

“Different.”

pages.alt: A friendly mole emerges from a mound beside the carrots, surprising Waffles.
pages.text:
The mole dusted off his paws.

“I’m just making a tunnel.”

Waffles’ ears perked up.

“A tunnel?”

“Yes.”

“Where does it go?”

The mole shrugged.

“Down.”

pages.alt: A friendly mole emerges from a mound beside the carrots, surprising Waffles.
pages.text:
Waffles smiled.

Pip immediately said,

“No.”

“I didn’t say anything.”

“You were thinking about going in.”

“I was not.”

“You absolutely were.”

Waffles looked into the hole.

“Maybe just one little—”

“No.”

They moved on.

pages.alt: Waffles wears his detective lettuce hat and inspects a ripe tomato while Pip watches.
pages.text:
Then they reached the strawberry patch.

Waffles stopped.

His nose twitched.

His eyes widened.

Pip landed in front of him.

“No.”

“I haven’t done anything.”

“You are thinking loudly.”

Waffles stared at the berries.

“One strawberry.”

“No.”

“Half a strawberry.”

“No.”

“A very small investigation bite?”

Pip folded her wings.

“Waffles.”

pages.alt: Waffles and Pip discover a squirrel eating sunflower seeds behind the beans.
pages.text:
Waffles looked away.

Then—

RUSTLE.

Both of them froze.

Something moved behind the beans.

RUSTLE.

Waffles whispered,

“The garden criminal.”

Pip whispered,

“Or the wind.”

RUSTLE.

pages.alt: Waffles and Pip discover a squirrel eating sunflower seeds behind the beans.
pages.text:
Waffles grabbed a stick.

Pip looked at it.

“What are you going to do with that?”

“Detective stick.”

“That is not a thing.”

“It is now.”

They crept closer.

Waffles tiptoed.

Pip fluttered quietly.

RUSTLE.

Closer.

Closer.

Closer.

pages.alt: Waffles and Pip discover a squirrel eating sunflower seeds behind the beans.
pages.text:
Waffles jumped around the corner.

“AHA!”

A squirrel sat beside a pile of sunflower seeds.

The squirrel froze.

Waffles froze.

Pip froze.

The squirrel slowly put one seed into his mouth.

Crunch.

pages.alt: Waffles and Pip discover a squirrel eating sunflower seeds behind the beans.
pages.text:
Waffles pointed dramatically.

“Caught!”

The squirrel swallowed.

“Caught doing what?”

Waffles looked at Pip.

Pip looked at the seeds.

“Eating sunflower seeds?”

The squirrel nodded.

“Yes.”

Waffles lowered his detective stick.

“Oh.”

The squirrel held out a seed.

“Want one?”

Waffles sniffed it.

“No thank you.”

pages.alt: Pip, the squirrel, and the mole laugh as Waffles discovers a carrot crumb on his chest.
pages.text:
Then Waffles suddenly gasped.

“My carrot!”

Pip looked at him.

“What carrot?”

“The carrot I brought for lunch.”

Pip sighed.

“Where did you put it?”

Waffles looked around.

He checked behind a pumpkin.

No carrot.

Under the lettuce.

No carrot.

Beside the tomatoes.

No carrot.

pages.alt: Pip, the squirrel, and the mole laugh as Waffles discovers a carrot crumb on his chest.
pages.text:
Waffles’ ears drooped.

“It’s gone.”

Pip stared at him.

“Waffles.”

“Yes?”

“Did you eat it?”

“No.”

“Are you sure?”

Waffles thought very hard.

Then he looked down.

A tiny orange piece of carrot was stuck in the fur on his chest.

Pip raised one eyebrow.

Waffles looked at it.

“Oh.”

pages.alt: Pip, the squirrel, and the mole laugh as Waffles discovers a carrot crumb on his chest.
pages.text:
Pip crossed her wings.

Waffles cleared his throat.

“I may have eaten the evidence.”

Pip burst out laughing.

The squirrel laughed.

Even the mole popped his head out of the ground and laughed.

Waffles looked around.

“This investigation is becoming very unprofessional.”

Pip landed on his head.

Right on top of the detective lettuce.

pages.alt: Pip, the squirrel, and the mole laugh as Waffles discovers a carrot crumb on his chest.
pages.text:
“So what did we learn?”

Waffles thought.

“The caterpillar ate the lettuce.”

Pip nodded.

“The mole dug the dirt.”

Pip nodded again.

“The squirrel ate the sunflower seeds.”

“Yes.”

Waffles smiled.

“And I ate my carrot.”

Pip laughed.

“Exactly.”

pages.alt: Waffles wears his detective lettuce hat and inspects a ripe tomato while Pip watches.
pages.text:
Waffles looked around the garden.

“So there was no garden criminal?”

“Nope.”

Waffles looked at the tomato.

The tomato sat quietly in the sunshine.

Waffles narrowed his eyes.

“I’m still watching you.”

Pip groaned.

And off they went—

one white rabbit detective,

one little blue bird assistant,

one innocent squirrel,

one innocent mole,

one relocated caterpillar,

and one tomato that Waffles still did not trust.

**The End**
